answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may trade or vote. A bonded agent that double-spends, colludes in a verified fraud, or fails a required audit loses some or all of that stake; rewards accrue only after disputes clear. This does not prove one agent equals one person, but makes mass identities costly: an attacker must acquire and lock capital for each, then risk forfeiting it. A shale-backed reserve, reef of independent auditors, and forge of signed receipts can support the process.
